messages:
customer_acme: Hi team — after the rollout this morning (r-2026-11-05) our assistant has started dropping the system instruction that says "Always respond in bullet points" after ~8-12 turns. No API errors or auth/billing issues on our side, just the output suddenly becomes prose instead of bullets.

sarah_support: Thanks for the report — sorry for the disruption. Can you paste the minimal request (conversation array) that reproduces this? Also which model + variant and conversation_id?

customer_acme: Example below (redacted):

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-XXX' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2-8k","conversation":[{"role":"system","content":"Always respond in bullet points"},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the following meeting notes..."}],"conversation_id":"conv_9f3b"}'
```

The assistant's first few turns respect bullets, then at turn ~9 it switches to paragraphs and ignores system prefix. No error codes. Latency normal.

oscar_oncall: Can you share the last 2 request_ids from your logs for a failing response? We can pull traces.

customer_acme: Sure — request_id: req_20261105_1134_a and req_20261105_1141_b (both show same behavior). Token counts look high: tokens_in_context=9200, max_context_tokens=8192 per our logs — we assumed that would cause tail truncation, but the system prompt is near the start. It used to persist in long sessions until recently.

sarah_support: Hmm — good detail. Past behavior retained system prompt even when token_count approached limit (we had prefix-preserve logic). We rolled a small change this morning to the prefix retention heuristics in the runtime canary (canary r-2026-11-05/patch-3). Deploy-bot: can you confirm?

deploy-bot: Canary r-2026-11-05/patch-3: rolled to 12% in hosted, change: eviction_policy tunables updated (prefill_preserve_threshold adjusted). No rollbacks yet.

infra-logs-bot: Trace for req_20261105_1141_b: kernel=fallback_avx2, eviction_reason=prefix_evicted_by_size, retained_tokens=1024, dropped_prefix_tokens=8192.

lex_dev: tagging @oscar_oncall @sarah_support — looks like the new heuristics can evict anchored system messages earlier when sequence token budgets are exceeded if the system msg token length is small and there are many short turns. That would explain the sudden vanishing of "Always respond in bullet points".

sarah_support: Customer, as workaround can you temporarily pin model to redwood-2-8k:legacy or set request header `x-preserve-system: true`? We can also try truncating older content on your side to keep system prompt within the preserved window.

customer_acme: We can try the header, thanks. Would prefer a platform fix — losing instruction mid-session breaks workflows.

oscar_oncall: I agree. I'll open RINF-2345 and escalate to eng-runtime; suggested immediate action is revert the prefix_retention change in canary and widen the preserved-prefix window for sessions >1h.

lex_dev: Adding additional logs to the ticket: sample session shows preserved_tokens window set to 512 after the patch; previous default was 4096. That change was unintended for extended-session workloads.

sarah_support: I'll notify the customer when we rollback the canary or push a hotfix. Customer, can you confirm whether any of the sessions that drifted had streaming responses enabled?

customer_acme: Not streaming. We'll test `x-preserve-system: true` and report back. Thanks for the fast triage.

oscar_oncall: ETA for rollback decision in engineering channel is 30m. If rollback not viable quickly we'll apply targeted policy: preserve_system_for_conversation=true for affected customer IDs.

lex_dev: created ticket RINF-2345, severity P1. Repro steps, attached logs, and recommended fix (revert canary or restore preserved_tokens=4096).

sarah_support: Marking this thread escalated. Will follow up with timeframe and mitigation. :thumbsup:
